question: Which picklist values differ between the support and finance case processes, field by field?
why: If nothing differs, the requirement is a layout or Dynamic Forms problem, not a record type.
answer_shape: The picklistValues blocks per record type, plus the evidence that a record type is warranted at all.
proposed_default: Two Case record types (Support, Billing) differing on Status/Reason; if only the reply address and queue differ, use one record type plus Origin-driven routing instead.

question: Is this object Lead, Opportunity, Solution, or Case?
why: Those four require a businessProcess; every other object forbids one, and both mistakes are deploy failures.
answer_shape: The object name, and whether a BusinessProcess file must ship with the record type.
proposed_default: Case — so a Support Process must be authored and deployed alongside every Case record type.

question: Which profile does each affected user actually hold?
why: Permission sets grant record-type visibility only; the default record type and the page layout assignment exist solely on Profile.
answer_shape: The profile x record type x layout matrix, not a per-record-type layout list.
proposed_default: Three profiles matching the three teams (Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing), each with an explicit default record type and layout assignment.

question: Do Cases already exist on any record type we are creating or retiring?
why: Reassignment blanks any picklist value absent from the target record type, silently.
answer_shape: The at-risk record count and the value-mapping step that must run first (zero is a valid answer, but it must be stated).
proposed_default: None — support runs from a shared mailbox today, so this is a greenfield Case model; confirm no legacy Cases exist in the org.

question: Is a field being marked Required on the layout meant to be enforced everywhere?
why: Layout Required binds to that layout only — API, Flow, and every other layout ignore it.
answer_shape: A decision between field-level required and a record-type-scoped validation rule, per field.
proposed_default: Priority and Origin enforced at field or validation-rule level, because Web-to-Case and Email-to-Case create Cases through the API, not through a layout.

question: Are Person Accounts enabled on this org?
why: Person Account record types are a separate model, and the Metadata API will not round-trip their custom picklist values.
answer_shape: Yes/no, plus a separate design track and a manual picklist verification step if yes.
proposed_default: No — Acme is B2B, so Cases hang off Business Accounts and Contacts.

question: What is on the current profile that has no permission-set equivalent?
why: loginHours, loginIpRanges, layoutAssignments, the default app and the default record type exist only on Profile. They are the residue, and the only reason a profile still exists.
answer_shape: The residue list — the exact contents of the base profile file.
proposed_default: A minimal base profile per team carrying only layout assignments, default app and default record type; every object, field and tab grant lives in permission sets.

question: Which users hold this profile, and do they all hold the same user licence?
why: A permission set with a LicenseId can only be assigned where the profile's UserLicenseId matches; a mixed-licence population must be split before, not after.
answer_shape: The population split by licence, and whether LicenseId should be left empty.
proposed_default: 18 internal users (12 Tier 1, 4 Tier 2, 2 Billing) on Salesforce licences with Service Cloud; leave LicenseId empty on the permission sets.

question: Which objects, fields, tabs, apps, record types, layouts and classes are in scope?
why: A profile retrieve returns permissions only for what else is in the same manifest. Without this list the retrieved profile is silently incomplete.
answer_shape: The package.xml that makes the retrieve honest, reused for the deploy.
proposed_default: Case, Account, Contact, EmailMessage, Entitlement, plus the Case record types, layouts and the Service app.

question: Are we adding access, or taking it away?
why: Permission sets only grant. Removing access means editing the profile explicitly to false, or muting inside a group — two mechanisms with different blast radii.
answer_shape: Additive or strip, and which mechanism applies.
proposed_default: Additive — this is a new Service Cloud footprint, so every grant is new and no strip phase is required.

question: Is the profile standard (custom=false) or custom?
why: Editing standard objects on standard profiles is disabled in API 50.0+, so the strip phase will not apply.
answer_shape: A clone-first decision, recorded before any deploy is attempted.
proposed_default: Clone Standard User into custom profiles before any deploy is attempted.

question: Who exactly does this work — an employee, a customer, a partner, or a contractor?
why: The answer selects a licence, and licence selects API allocation, object access and portal template long before design starts.
answer_shape: A licence_implication value, and an escalation to architect/license-optimization-strategy if the answer is not an employee.
proposed_default: Employees only — 18 internal support and finance staff; the customer portal is explicitly out of scope for this phase.

question: When you say only Finance sees billing cases — can others not open the record at all, or can they open it but should not see a field on it?
why: Record access and field access are different mechanisms configured in different places; record access itself is seven ordered layers.
answer_shape: A sharing_impact value naming the layer — OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rule, team, manual/Apex, restriction — plus a separate FLS row.

question: What must NOT happen automatically, and who fixes it when the automation is wrong?
why: "Make it automatic" hides the trigger, the condition, the exception path and the owner of the failure.
answer_shape: The exception path and a named owner, which is what makes the automation row estimable.

question: Which channels create cases, at what steady-state volume, and what is the biggest single batch anyone would ever push?
why: Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual entry have different limits, routing behaviour and spam exposure; and automation that passes UAT on ten records fails on a bulk load, because Flow and Apex share the transaction limits.
answer_shape: A channel inventory with the daily limit and pending-queue risk for each, plus a steady-state number and a worst-case batch number.
proposed_default: Email-to-Case ~400/day (support@ and billing@), Web-to-Case ~60/day, manual ~20/day, no phone; no bulk Case load is planned, so the worst-case batch is the daily email peak.

question: What must happen in the first minute: owner, acknowledgement, calendar, priority?
why: Assignment, auto-response, business hours and priority all resolve during the save; anything set later runs on the wrong clock.
answer_shape: The before-save Flow scope and the assignment-rule design, stated as an ordered list of what happens during the save.
proposed_default: All four in the first minute: assignment rule sets the owner, auto-response sends the acknowledgement with the case number, a before-save Flow stamps Case.BusinessHoursId, and priority is mapped from the form field or the mailbox.

question: Which public addresses do customers actually write to, and does the same mailbox forward to more than one place?
why: Each address is one routingAddresses element; a mailbox that forwards twice duplicates every case, and two elements sharing an emailAddress have no deterministic configuration.
answer_shape: The channel list with one forwarding rule each, checked by the duplicate-address ERROR in the skill's checker.
proposed_default: Two routing addresses: support@acme.example and billing@acme.example, each forwarding to exactly one Salesforce routing address.

question: Which queue owns each channel's cases?
why: caseOwner on a routing address writes the org-level defaultCaseOwner, so a second address setting it overwrites the first.
answer_shape: Ownership expressed as caseOrigin per address plus assignment rule entries, not as caseOwner.
proposed_default: Express ownership as caseOrigin per address plus assignment-rule entries: support@ -> Tier 1 queue, billing@ -> Billing queue; leave caseOwner unset on both addresses.

question: Is the Case.Origin picklist value for each channel already active in the org?
why: caseOrigin is the only per-address value an assignment rule can read; a value not in the picklist stamps something nobody can filter on.
answer_shape: The picklist additions that must deploy before or with the settings file.
proposed_default: Add Email-Support, Email-Billing and Web as active Case.Origin values, deployed before or with the Case settings file.

question: Is this org on Lightning Threading or legacy threading?
why: Two mutually exclusive pairs of token switches exist and the wrong pair is inert.
answer_shape: The one pair of threading switches to set, plus useEmailHeadersForThreading as the gateway fallback.

question: What should happen to mail we refuse — bounce it or drop it?
why: unauthorizedSenderAction and overEmailLimitAction both accept Discard, which leaves no Case, no EmailMessage and no bounce.
answer_shape: A deliberate Bounce / Requeue choice per action instead of an invisible failure mode.
proposed_default: Bounce on unauthorised sender and Requeue on over-limit, so refused mail leaves a trace.

question: Who sends the acknowledgement, and does that address forward back to us?
why: Any auto-response sender that reaches a routing address is an unbounded case-creation loop; so is a vacation responder on the forwarding mailbox.
answer_shape: A no-reply sender, plus the mail-server rule audit the checker cannot see.
proposed_default: A no-reply org-wide address sends the acknowledgement; support@ and billing@ are reply addresses only, and the mail-server rules are audited for auto-forward before go-live.

question: Does anyone need email headers for a future security investigation?
why: saveEmailHeaders captures envelope data at processing time and cannot be backfilled.
answer_shape: Headers on or off from day one, and whether EmailMessage.Headers is inside the retention scope.
proposed_default: Yes — enable saveEmailHeaders from day one and confirm EmailMessage.Headers sits inside the org's retention scope.

question: How do Cases arrive: web form, email, UI, API, Data Loader, Flow?
why: Only the web and email intake channels invoke the assignment rule by default; every other channel must opt in.
answer_shape: The channel matrix, and the header or checkbox each non-default channel must set.
proposed_default: Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case invoke it by default; manual UI creation needs the Assign using active assignment rule checkbox defaulted on for the Case layouts.

question: Which field values decide the owner, and are they set at save time?
why: Criteria read values at save; formulas and after-save Flows are not there yet.
answer_shape: The routing fields, each confirmed to be populated by the intake before assignment runs.
proposed_default: Case.Origin (stamped by the routing address) and the Account's support tier — both present at save; do not route on a formula or an after-save Flow result.

question: Queue or person, and what happens when nobody matches?
why: Person targets break on leave and departures; unmatched records go to the default owner silently.
answer_shape: Queue targets per entry and an explicit catch-all entry naming the fall-through owner.
proposed_default: Queue targets only (Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing), plus a catch-all final entry routing to the Tier 1 queue.

question: Does anything else write OwnerId after save?
why: After-save Flows, triggers, Omni-Channel and escalation all overwrite the assignment rule's result.
answer_shape: One authoritative writer at creation, plus the list of later writers and when each fires.
proposed_default: Omni-Channel push and the 8-business-hour escalation both write OwnerId after save; name the assignment rule as the single authoritative writer at creation and document the two later handoffs.

question: Should the customer get an acknowledgement, and on which channels?
why: Auto-response fires only when the assignment rule fires, from a verified org-wide address.
answer_shape: The per-channel acknowledgement decision, and the verified org-wide address each one sends from.
proposed_default: Yes on Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case, with the case number in the body; auto-response wired to the same channels as the assignment rule rather than bolted on later.

question: Who works each pool, and how does that membership list change?
why: Named users churn; roles and public groups maintain themselves.
answer_shape: Membership expressed as a group or role that survives onboarding and offboarding, per queue.
proposed_default: Tier 1 membership changes monthly, so make the Tier 1 queue's member a public group (or role) rather than 12 named users; Tier 2 and Billing are small and stable enough for either.

question: Which objects will each queue own?
why: A queue owns only the objects in queueSobject; rules and Omni-Channel targeting it for another object fail.
answer_shape: One queue per work pool, each with its queueSobject list.
proposed_default: Case only, on all three queues — this phase has no Lead, no chat and no telephony work item.

question: Is Omni-Channel pushing from this queue?
why: Without a routing configuration the queue is a list view.
answer_shape: Per queue: pushed by Omni-Channel, or worked as a list view.
proposed_default: Tier 1 yes (work is pushed); Tier 2 and Billing no — they pick from the queue list view.

question: Which objects are pushed, and does capacity release on close or on tab close?
why: One service channel per object; capacityModel decides when an agent frees up.
answer_shape: One service channel per pushed object, each with an explicit capacityModel value.

question: How many items can a Tier 1 agent hold, and how much is each case worth?
why: Presence configuration capacity versus routing configuration capacityWeight.
answer_shape: A capacity number per presence configuration and a capacityWeight per work item type.

question: Least active or most available, and what is the tie-breaker?
why: routingModel plus secondaryRoutingPriorityField decide push order.
answer_shape: A routingModel value plus the secondaryRoutingPriorityField, stated so agents can explain the order.

question: What happens when nobody accepts a pushed case?
why: pushTimeout and presenceStatusOnPushTimeout decide whether the item loops to the same agent.
answer_shape: A pushTimeout value and the presence status the agent is moved to, so nothing stalls silently.

question: Who receives pushed work, by profile or by user?
why: Presence configuration assignments is the only way an agent enters Omni-Channel.
answer_shape: The presence configuration's assignments list, expressed so it survives monthly membership churn.
proposed_default: By profile — the Tier 1 profile — because Tier 1 membership changes monthly and per-user assignment would drift.

question: Skills-based or queue-based routing, and is the feature enabled?
why: Skills-based routing is a separate enablement with extra records.
answer_shape: The routing family chosen, and the enablement state of the feature it needs, before any metadata is written.
proposed_default: Queue-based — the requirement describes three team queues and no skill dimension.

question: Which SLA promise are we making, and to whom: one business day, four working hours, calendar hours?
why: Fixes whether business time is needed at all and which consumers must read it.
answer_shape: The consumer map: which escalation entries, milestones and Apex read which calendar, per promise.
proposed_default: Premier accounts: first response within 4 business hours. Standard accounts: within 1 business day. Both on business time, not calendar time; Severity 1 is 24/7 calendar time.

question: Which regions or teams work different hours or observe different holidays?
why: Each distinct answer is a calendar.
answer_shape: The calendar list, each with a time zone and a holiday set.
proposed_default: Two calendars plus a 24/7 default: EMEA (Europe/London, 08:00-18:00), US (America/New_York, 08:00-20:00), each with its own regional holiday set.

question: How do we know a Case's region at creation?
why: Decides the Case.BusinessHoursId rule; if unknowable at creation, the design falls back to the default.
answer_shape: The before-save Flow logic that stamps Case.BusinessHoursId, and its fallback when the region is unknowable.

question: Do reports or code need elapsed working time?
why: Formulas cannot compute elapsed business time; Apex diff can.
answer_shape: A decision to build (or not build) the Apex business-hours helper, with the reports that depend on it named.

question: Does the clock start at case creation, or restart every time anyone edits the case?
why: escalationStartTime is CaseCreation or CaseLastModified; disableEscalationWhenModified is a separate lever that stops escalation on edit.
answer_shape: The per-tier choice of both fields, plus the list of automations that count as an "edit".
proposed_default: CaseCreation for the 8-business-hour Tier 2 escalation, because the requirement measures from creation, not from last touch; leave disableEscalationWhenModified off.

question: Which calendar does each escalation tier follow, and is there a tier that must run 24/7?
why: businessHoursSource is None, Case or Static per entry — a per-Case calendar design is defeated by an entry left on None.
answer_shape: One businessHoursSource value per entry, with the Severity 1 exception written down as a decision.
proposed_default: businessHoursSource = Case for the 8-business-hour entry (so it follows the Case's regional calendar); a separate Severity 1 entry with businessHoursSource = None for the 24/7 promise.

question: Which escalation or assignment rule is active in production today, and who owns it?
why: Activating a new rule is a cutover, not an addition — activating yours silently deactivates theirs.
answer_shape: The incumbent rule's name and entries, and a named owner to sign off the swap (or a confirmed "none").
proposed_default: None — support runs from a shared mailbox, so there is no incumbent rule; confirm the org has no legacy Case rule already active.

question: When the escalation timer expires, do we notify, change the owner, or both?
why: Reassignment writes OwnerId and re-fires record automation; notify-only does not.
answer_shape: A per-threshold action table, plus the automation blast radius of any reassign action.
proposed_default: Both: reassign to the Tier 2 queue and notify, because the requirement says untouched cases "escalate to Tier 2" — but record the automation blast radius of the OwnerId write.

question: What is the SLA in minutes, and has anyone signed off on the engine's batching latency?
why: minutesToEscalation is stored in minutes while Setup shows hours, and the engine fires in batches.
answer_shape: An agreed minutes value with headroom, not an hours value transcribed as minutes.
proposed_default: 8 business hours = 480 minutes, with headroom agreed for batch latency; write 480, not 8.

question: How do we cut over without a wave of instant escalations?
why: Cases already past their threshold escalate on the first pass after activation.
answer_shape: A deploy-inactive-then-activate plan with a defined comparison window.
proposed_default: Deploy the rule inactive, then activate inside a defined comparison window once the sandbox proof is signed off.

question: How does a case get its entitlement, on each intake channel we run?
why: An entitlement process only runs on a case that carries an entitlement; Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case do not supply one.
answer_shape: The per-channel automation list, and the fallback for cases with no account.
proposed_default: A before-save or after-save automation stamps EntitlementId from the Contact's Account on all three channels, with a documented fallback for cases with no matching account.

question: What ends the commitment — the case closing, or something we stamp ourselves?
why: Exit criteria are the boundary for recurrence, so Status = Closed restarts every non-recurring milestone on a reopen.
answer_shape: The exit-criteria filter, and an explicit decision on whether reopens are new commitments.

question: Who or what marks the first-response milestone complete?
why: Nothing completes a milestone; CaseMilestone.CompletionDate has to be written.
answer_shape: Either satisfiable completion criteria, or the named Apex/Flow that stamps the date.
proposed_default: Satisfiable completion criteria on the first outbound EmailMessage, or a Flow that stamps CompletionDate — chosen explicitly, not assumed.

question: Which calendar wins: the entitlement process, the milestone, or the Case?
why: Three calendars can disagree, and milestones read none of Case.BusinessHoursId by default.
answer_shape: One named calendar authority per SLA policy, plus every milestone-level override written down.
proposed_default: The Case's calendar is the authority for the first-response SLA; set the process and milestone calendars to match it explicitly rather than relying on a default.

question: Do we ever stop the SLA clock, and who is allowed to?
why: Case.IsStopped is writable by anything with edit access, and stopped time is hidden unless a setting is on.
answer_shape: A stop policy, FLS on Case.IsStopped, and enableMilestoneStoppedTime set before go-live.

question: Do the same milestones serve more than one tier?
why: Recurrence lives on the shared MilestoneType, so one edit changes every process that names it.
answer_shape: The milestone-type-to-process map, and any type that needs splitting.
proposed_default: Premier and Standard share one First Response milestone type but need different time triggers — check whether that forces two milestone types before authoring either.

question: Which field does the user actually edit to cause this — the one on the Case, or a child record?
why: Validation rules do not fire on a parent when a child record changes it, so a rule guarding a parent field never runs in a child-driven process.
answer_shape: The right object for each rule, or a decision to use a record-triggered flow on the child instead.

question: Is any workflow field update or automation writing this field after save?
why: Custom validation rules are not re-run after a workflow field update re-saves the record, so the rule is not a database invariant.
answer_shape: Either a migration of that field update to a before-save flow, or an explicit acceptance that violating records will exist.

question: Which users and integrations must be able to save a Case the rule would reject?
why: Every rule with no bypass blocks every data load and every API write that does not meet the condition.
answer_shape: The Custom Permission name and the Permission Set that carries it.
proposed_default: Email-to-Case and Web-to-Case both create Cases through the API — carry a Custom Permission bypass on an integration permission set so intake is never blocked by a rule aimed at agents.

question: Is the field the error should attach to on every layout for every Case record type in scope?
why: errorDisplayField silently changes to Top of Page when the field is not visible on the layout.
answer_shape: Either a confirmed layout per record type, or an error message written to read correctly at the top of the page.

question: Does the data already violate this rule today?
why: Validation rules fire on update as well as insert, so an active rule on dirty data blocks every edit of every violating record.
answer_shape: A decision to deploy with active=false and a named cleanup owner, or a count proving the data is clean.
proposed_default: No existing Cases, so the data is clean by construction; still deploy any rule aimed at migrated Accounts or Contacts inactive until a count proves it.

question: Does the formula touch an address, a person name, or a dependent picklist?
why: Validation rules cannot use compound fields as of API version 20.0.
answer_shape: A rewrite against the component fields, done before the formula is authored.
proposed_default: Rewrite against the component fields (BillingStreet, BillingCity, FirstName, LastName) before anyone starts typing.

question: Who does each email come from, who may send from that address, and who answers replies?
why: Sender identity is an org-wide email address that must exist and be verified in every org, with profile restrictions on who may use it.
answer_shape: One verified org-wide address per outbound flow, with the profiles allowed to send from it and the mailbox that receives replies.
proposed_default: General case replies from support@acme.example, finance replies from billing@acme.example, acknowledgements from a no-reply address — all three verified org-wide addresses, restricted to the profiles that need them.

question: Is each template used by a rule (assignment, auto-response, escalation) or by Flow?
why: Rules deployed by metadata reference Classic templates only.
answer_shape: The template type per consumer, decided before the template is written.
proposed_default: The acknowledgement and escalation templates are rule-driven, so they must be Classic templates; anything Flow-driven may be Lightning.

question: Which record is the merge context for each template: Case, Lead, Contact?
why: Merge fields resolve only for the firing record and its parents.
answer_shape: The merge context object per template, plus the parent chain the merge fields rely on.
proposed_default: Case, with Contact and Account as parents — the acknowledgement needs the case number, so it merges from Case.

question: Could the same event fire twice and send two emails?
why: Duplicate automation is the usual cause of duplicate email.
answer_shape: One event, one email — the event-to-email map with any duplicate path removed.
proposed_default: One acknowledgement per case creation: auto-response only, with no parallel Flow email alert on the same event.

question: Does Email-to-Case threading depend on a token in this email?
why: Removing the thread reference breaks reply threading.
answer_shape: Per template: whether it carries the thread token, and the threading test that proves replies land on the case.
proposed_default: Keep the thread token in every customer-facing Case template so replies land on the case rather than opening a new one.

question: What number do you need out of this, and what has to appear on the same row as it?
why: Reporting requirements assume joins the report-type rules forbid; a four-object chain is the ceiling.
answer_shape: A reporting row naming the base object, the join chain, and whether rows must appear with no related record.

question: Where does this data live right now — in Salesforce, or in another system?
why: A requirement sourced from an ERP or billing system is an integration requirement wearing a validation-rule costume, and needs a pattern decision before sizing.
answer_shape: An integration row naming direction, volume, latency tolerance, and the integration-pattern-selection branch.
proposed_default: The website form is the only external producer named; confirm whether it posts to Web-to-Case directly or through middleware, and whether account/entitlement data comes from a billing system.

question: Walk me through what the support team does today — what do you type, where, and what do you do next?
why: Stakeholders describe the workaround they built around the legacy tool as if it were the requirement.
answer_shape: An As-Is step list where each step is tagged keep / drop / replace, so the To-Be is not a re-implementation of the shared mailbox.

question: How will we know case intake works before customers do?
why: Threading, auto-response loops and truncation only show up under real email.
answer_shape: A clock test, a threading test and a loop test, each with a stated expected result in the sandbox.
proposed_default: Three named sandbox tests before go-live: an SLA clock test across a weekend, a reply-threading test, and an auto-response loop test from a forwarding mailbox.

question: What is the org's actual sandbox allocation, and how much of it is already spent?
why: Enterprise Edition ships zero Developer Pro and zero Full sandboxes; a higher-tier licence may already be consumed by a lower-tier sandbox.
answer_shape: A real licence budget per sandbox type, with what is already provisioned against it.

question: Which environments will hold copied production records, and who may read them?
why: Only Partial Copy and Full copy data; that answer decides where masking, a post-copy class and access review are mandatory.
answer_shape: The subset of rows that need a SandboxPostCopy class rather than a note, plus who may read them.

question: What is the longest refresh floor any environment in the ladder has to respect?
why: The Full sandbox's 29-day floor is the constraint the release calendar must bend around, not the other way round.
answer_shape: A refresh calendar whose cells are all achievable against each type's floor.

question: Which objects must a Partial Copy template select, and who decides?
why: A Partial Copy cannot be created at all until a template exists, and the template silently defines what QA can test.
answer_shape: A named template owner and an object list, agreed before the licence is consumed.
proposed_default: At minimum Account, Contact, Case, Entitlement and EmailMessage, so the intake and SLA paths are testable end to end.

question: What does the post-copy automation have to do, and can the Automated Process user do it?
why: The post-copy class runs as an invisible user with incomplete object access — scrubs written naively fail quietly.
answer_shape: A class scoped to what that user can actually reach, plus a manual fallback for what it cannot.

question: Which settings, endpoints and credentials must never point at production after a copy?
why: Integration endpoints and scheduled jobs survive a refresh still aimed at live systems.
answer_shape: The seed values the post-copy class writes, per environment.
proposed_default: The Email-to-Case routing addresses and the website form endpoint must be re-pointed on every refresh, or the sandbox will answer real customer mail.

question: Which sandbox is UAT in, when was it last refreshed, and is another refresh booked inside the window?
why: A refresh during UAT deletes the build and the seeded data; a Full sandbox's 29-day floor makes teams book refreshes far in advance and forget them.
answer_shape: refreshed_on and build_deployed_on in the plan header, plus a named person who can veto a refresh.

question: Does any acceptance criterion depend on data volume — a rollup, a queue backlog, a query, a batch?
why: A Partial Copy holds a sample, so volume-dependent behaviour cannot be proved in it.
answer_shape: The sandbox type decision, and an explicit list of cases the chosen environment cannot prove.
proposed_default: Yes — 400 emails a day against the Email-to-Case daily limit and the Tier 1 queue backlog; list the cases the chosen sandbox type cannot prove.

question: Which named user, with which profile and permission sets, runs each test case?
why: An admin bypasses FLS and most sharing in the UI, so an admin pass proves nothing about the persona.
answer_shape: A persona table with real usernames — the roster the sign-off record is anchored to.
proposed_default: One named tester per team — Tier 1, Tier 2, Billing — on the real profile and permission sets, never the admin.

question: Does any criterion involve an email arriving, and who has to receive it?
why: Sandboxes default to System Email Only, and only User.Email is .invalid-suffixed on refresh — Contact and Lead emails are real.
answer_shape: A deliverability setting recorded with a date, and scrubbed contact emails before it is raised.
proposed_default: Yes — the acknowledgement is a core promise, so raise deliverability deliberately and scrub Contact emails before doing so.

question: How will test data be created — UI, Data Loader, Bulk API, REST?
why: The three load paths disagree about whether assignment rules run at all.
answer_shape: The tool and its assignment-rule setting written into the case preconditions, with a UI control record to compare against.

question: Which criteria are restrictions rather than capabilities — what must be blocked, hidden, or rejected?
why: A script built only from "the user can..." never touches a validation rule, FLS or sharing.
answer_shape: At least one negative_path case per story, and a go decision that is invalid without them.
proposed_default: At minimum: Tier 1 must not see billing cases if that is the intent, and an unauthorised sender's mail must bounce rather than create a case.

question: For each expected result, what would the tester actually look at — a screen, a query, a mailbox, a file?
why: The oracle decides the evidence type and the automation verdict; a then clause with no observable is not testable.
answer_shape: An evidence entry per case and an automation_candidate of apex, flow-test or none.

question: For every deny case: what is the persona set up without, and is anything else already blocking it?
why: A permission set can grant but never deny, and a scoping rule empties a list view without removing access.
answer_shape: A deny that is attributable to a named mechanism rather than to a coincidence.

question: Which UI does each persona actually use — Lightning desktop, the mobile app, or Classic?
why: formFactor is what selects the override the persona sees, and the three values are different pages.
answer_shape: A precondition per case naming the form factor, with steps runnable by the person assigned them.
proposed_default: Lightning desktop for all three teams; no mobile requirement is stated in this phase.

question: Is the expected result reachable through the path the persona uses, or only through the one the admin used?
why: UI-created records and API-loaded records go through different halves of the save order; layout-level rules run for one and not the other.
answer_shape: A separate case per load path, not one case that quietly proves the easier half.
proposed_default: Test each of the three intake channels separately — Email-to-Case, Web-to-Case and manual UI — rather than proving the easy half once.

question: Which reports, list views, and Flow entry criteria filter on this record type today?
why: Report filters key on the label, which is not stable; code and Flows key on DeveloperName, which is.
answer_shape: The rename blast radius, enumerated before anyone renames anything.
proposed_default: None today; fix DeveloperName values now so the later rename blast radius is zero.

question: Does a managed package require this profile to be assigned?
why: Some packages ship profile-dependent configuration that a permission set cannot replace.
answer_shape: A documented exception list, or confirmation that the package ships its own permission sets.
proposed_default: None known; confirm against the org's installed-package list before the access step runs.

question: Who verifies access afterwards, and against what?
why: "It deployed" is not evidence. Effective access is the union of the profile and every assigned permission set, visible per user in Setup.
answer_shape: A named verification step: a View Summary check plus the assignment-count SOQL.
proposed_default: The CRM admin lead runs a View Summary check on one user per team plus the assignment-count query, before UAT opens.

question: Who should be notified of a new record: shared mailbox, every member, nobody?
why: email and doesSendEmailToMembers are independent switches.
answer_shape: Per queue: the notification address, and whether member email is on.
proposed_default: A shared mailbox per queue rather than every member, so notifications are read rather than filtered.

question: What happens to queue-owned records when a queue is retired?
why: Records owned by a retired queue are stranded.
answer_shape: A retirement step in the runbook, with the reassignment target named.
proposed_default: A retirement step in the runbook: reassign open Cases to the surviving queue before the queue is deleted.

question: Who maintains next year's holidays, and when?
why: Holidays expire; unmaintained calendars silently stop pausing.
answer_shape: An owner and a yearly deploy slot in the release calendar.
proposed_default: A named owner in Service Operations, with a yearly holiday deploy booked in the release calendar each Q4.

question: How will we know next month that the escalation rule still fires?
why: IsEscalated is a plain writable boolean, not an engine-owned lock — nothing reports on a rule that quietly stopped.
answer_shape: A saved report or query on escalated, still-open cases, with an owner and a cadence.
proposed_default: A saved report on escalated, still-open Cases, reviewed weekly by the Tier 2 lead.

question: Is entitlement versioning on, and who owns the next version?
why: The version fields do nothing until the org switch is on, and an SLA change means a new file with every time-trigger offset re-derived.
answer_shape: The versioning switch state and a named owner for version bumps.

question: Does each message fit in 255 characters and name both the problem and the fix?
why: errorMessage is capped at 255 characters; a rule that cannot say what to do generates a support ticket per occurrence.
answer_shape: The final message text per rule, under 255 characters, naming both the problem and the fix.
proposed_default: Write the final message text at design time, not a placeholder to be filled in at deploy time.

question: Who owns each environment, and who approves its refresh?
why: An environment with no owner is the one that gets refreshed over someone's uncommitted work.
answer_shape: A named owner per environment, and a separate named approver for its refresh.
proposed_default: A named owner per row of the topology table, with the data owner (not the refresher) accountable for approving a refresh.

question: When must the validation deploy run relative to sign-off, and who accepts a deferred defect?
why: A quick deploy only skips tests within 10 days of a successful validation, so a validation taken at the start of a three-week cycle is dead by sign-off.
answer_shape: A dated validation slot in the plan, and a named business owner for the known-issues list.

question: Which permission set or group carries the feature, and is its recalculation finished?
why: PermissionSetGroup.Status is a real picklist — Outdated or Updating means the tester does not yet have what the script assumes.
answer_shape: A pre-run gate query, and the PSG each persona depends on.
proposed_default: A pre-run gate query on PermissionSetGroup.Status before each UAT session, so a false-fail is not logged as a build defect.

question: When a test case fails, who decides Fail versus Blocked?
why: Blocked is an environment result and must not raise a defect against the build; conflating them corrupts the defect data.
answer_shape: A named triager and a re-runnable run sheet.
proposed_default: A named triager (the QA or BA lead) with a run sheet whose rows are re-runnable rather than overwritten.
